credentials.description: clientId (API key), provided in the Djomy merchant space
clientSecret (secret key), provided in the Djomy merchant space

parameters.name: transactionId
parameters.description: The transactionId returned by create_payment or create_payment_gateway. Passed as a path parameter.

example_prompt: Add server-side Djomy payment verification to my order fulfillment flow.

response_schema.description: All responses are wrapped in { success, message, data, error, errors, timestamp, status }.

status.description: Use status === 'SUCCESS' as the only safe condition to fulfill an order.

receivedAmount.description: Amount received by the merchant after Djomy fees.

currency.description: Note: these are Djomy's internal currency strings, not ISO 4217 codes.

providerReference.description: Reference from the payment operator (Orange Money, Kulu, etc.).

gotchas: Never fulfill an order until data.status === 'SUCCESS'. PENDING means the payer has not confirmed yet. Djomy's docs list AUTHORIZED and CAPTURED for create_payment and create_payment_gateway (AUTHORIZED marked « A ignorer pour le moment »), for payment links (both marked « à ignorer pour le moment ») and in the V2 webhook's data.payment.status, not for this endpoint: treat any status other than SUCCESS as unpaid, and don't reject a value outside the enum.

The transactionId comes from your create_payment / create_payment_gateway record, from the signed webhook (check X-Webhook-Signature first), or from a request: after a payment link, Djomy adds transactionId to the returnUrl (CreatePaymentLinkRequest.returnUrl: « Djomy rajoutera en paramètre d'url … transactionId et le status »). Prefer your own record: the example encodes the value with encodeURIComponent, so a visitor's "../…" stays in this endpoint's path instead of sending your access token and X-API-KEY to another endpoint, but a value of exactly ".." still climbs one level. The path parameter is typed only as a string; the transactionId Djomy returns is a uuid (CreatedPaymentDto and GetPaymentDto: "format": "uuid"), and the endpoint documents a 400 "Format de référence de transaction invalide".
receivedAmount is what you actually receive after Djomy deducts fees. Use this for your accounting, not paidAmount.
The currency field returns non-ISO strings: 'GNF', 'FCFA', 'Dollar', 'Leones'. Map these to ISO 4217 codes (GNF, XOF, USD, SLE) in your system.
A missing or invalid X-API-KEY returns HTTP 401 (documented as "Clé API manquante ou invalide").
open_questions: Production base URL: Djomy's API reference lists only https://sandbox-api.djomy.africa ("Staging environment"). Ask the user or Djomy for the production URL — never guess it.

Which status does a timed-out or refunded payment return here? The webhook has payment.timeout and payment.refunded events, but this endpoint's docs (GetPaymentDto.status) list only CREATED, PENDING, FAILED, SUCCESS, REDIRECTED and CANCELLED; the TIMEOUT and REFUNDED values this spec listed until now had no source.
